stories.headline: Our newest AI Quest: Mapping the human brain
stories.summary: Skip to main content Innovation & AI Products & platforms Company news Feed Newsletter Home Products & Platforms Products Learning & Education Our newest AI Quest: Mapping the human brain Oct 26, 2026 2 min read Our third lesson in our AI Quests series, “Polar Peaks,” teaches students key AI literacy skills while delving into neuroscience. Ronit Levavi Morad Senior Director, Google Research Share Listen to article [[duration]] minutes Read AI-generated summary Today, we’re launching “Polar Peaks”, our third quest in the AI Quests series, created by Google Research and the Stanford Accelerator for Learning to teach students how AI works and how to use it responsibly.
stories.why_it_matters: AI Quests invites students ages 11 to 14 to step into the shoes of Google researchers to tackle some of humanity’s biggest challenges. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in ai & machine learning.
key_points: Problem & Context: Polar Peaks: A journey to map the human brain In the first two quests, students tackle flood forecasting and eye disease detection, inspired by Google Research’s Flood Forecasting initiative and AI model for diabetic retinopathy screening.
Technical Implementation: They complete tasks like data cleaning and model testing, learning firsthand that AI requires careful human oversight and critical thinking.
Deployment & Impact: See more Training modules: Tools for teaching AI literacy Teachers play a critical role in bringing the quests to life and fitting them into their existing classroom curriculum.

stories.headline: Raising the quality of insights in agentic analytics
stories.summary: In just a few years, generative AI has changed the face of enterprise analytics, notably by making analytics accessible to users across the organization. Agentic AI promises to do even more, by automating entire workflows and taking actions based on agent insights.
stories.why_it_matters: But there is a problem: The quality of insights that agents currently generate leaves much to be desired. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in ai & machine learning.
key_points: Problem & Context: In just a few years, generative AI has changed the face of enterprise analytics, notably by making analytics accessible to users across the organization.
Technical Implementation: On average, 48% of insights generated by analytics agents at the surveyed companies lead to actions that improve the business.
Deployment & Impact: That is a marked advance from the 37% average the respondents say generated such actions one year ago.

stories.headline: Stop counting tokens, start counting what ships
stories.summary: When a developer gives an AI agent a coding task, the agent does more than answer once. It plans, generates code, runs tests, and repeats the process to correct errors.
stories.why_it_matters: A single task can use 10 to 50 times more tokens than a basic chat prompt. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in ai & machine learning.
key_points: Problem & Context: It plans, generates code, runs tests, and repeats the process to correct errors.

stories.headline: Why large dogs age faster than small ones, and other October research highlights
stories.summary: It’s a regrettable reality that there is never enough time to cover all the interesting scientific stories we come across. So every month, we highlight a handful of the best stories that nearly slipped through the cracks.
stories.why_it_matters: October’s list includes an epigenetic mechanism for why large dogs age faster than smaller ones; physicists who trapped a single particle of antimatter for months; and invisible tattoo inks that only show up under UV light. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in developers.
key_points: Problem & Context: Dogs, however, buck this pattern; larger dogs tend to age faster and die younger than smaller ones, which makes canines an ideal model for biologists to study to learn more about aging in general.

Technical Implementation: The authors used data from 864 dogs collected in the Dog Aging Project to map patterns of DNA methylation (which influences how much certain genes are turned on or off) across the entire genome.

Deployment & Impact: October’s list includes an epigenetic mechanism for why large dogs age faster than smaller ones; physicists who trapped a single particle of antimatter for months; and invisible tattoo inks that only show up under UV light.

stories.headline: Meta Andromeda: Powering the Next Generation of Ads Retrieval Through Model-System Co-Design
stories.summary: Skip to content Search this site Open Source Platforms Infrastructure Systems Physical Infrastructure Video Engineering & AR/VR Artificial Intelligence Watch Videos POSTED ON OCTOBER 28, 2026 TO ML APPLICATIONS, PRODUCTION ENGINEERING Meta Andromeda: Powering the Next Generation of Ads Retrieval Through Model-System Co-Design By Haiyu Lu, Shuo Gu, Yang Yang (Tony), Jingwen Ren, Tianchen Ji, Qing Zhang, Wentian Guo, Haocheng Wu, Siqi Zeng, Yunchen Pu, Liang Wang, Chonglin Sun This post describes the next generation of Meta Andromeda, Meta’s personalized ads retrieval engine, and how co-designing the model, system, and GPU hardware unlocks a new efficiency frontier for ads retrieval. In production, the system scores every eligible ad with near ranking-level model performance at retrieval scale and surfaces the top candidates at over one billion ads per second, a new throughput benchmark for ads retrieval-stage models (i.e., a 100x lift compared to the 2024 Meta Andromeda system).
stories.why_it_matters: For advertisers, this means better performance automatically from the retrieval system matching ads across a larger candidate pool, within the same latency budget. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in big tech.
key_points: Problem & Context: Skip to content Search this site Open Source Platforms Infrastructure Systems Physical Infrastructure Video Engineering & AR/VR Artificial Intelligence Watch Videos POSTED ON OCTOBER 28, 2026 TO ML APPLICATIONS, PRODUCTION ENGINEERING Meta Andromeda: Powering the Next Generation of Ads Retrieval Through Model-System Co-Design By Haiyu Lu, Shuo Gu, Yang Yang (Tony), Jingwen Ren, Tianchen Ji, Qing Zhang, Wentian Guo, Haocheng Wu, Siqi Zeng, Yunchen Pu, Liang Wang, Chonglin Sun This post describes the next generation of Meta Andromeda, Meta’s personalized ads retrieval engine, and how co-designing the model, system, and GPU hardware unlocks a new efficiency frontier for ads retrieval.

Technical Implementation: In production, the system scores every eligible ad with near ranking-level model performance at retrieval scale and surfaces the top candidates at over one billion ads per second, a new throughput benchmark for ads retrieval-stage models (i.e., a 100x lift compared to the 2024 Meta Andromeda system).
Deployment & Impact: For advertisers, this means better performance automatically from the retrieval system matching ads across a larger candidate pool, within the same latency budget.

stories.headline: Making Failure Diagnosis Reliable with Pensive AI
stories.summary: By Praneeth Yenugutala , Victor Dusa , Anastasia Samoilova , Megan Ren , Justin Wei , Marcelo Mayworm At Netflix, data and machine learning practitioners run millions of workloads each day across orchestration systems and compute engines such as Titus, Spark, Trino, and Druid. On peak days, roughly 100,000 workloads fail.
stories.why_it_matters: When workloads fail, the failure itself is only the beginning. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in big tech.
key_points: Problem & Context: By Praneeth Yenugutala , Victor Dusa , Anastasia Samoilova , Megan Ren , Justin Wei , Marcelo Mayworm At Netflix, data and machine learning practitioners run millions of workloads each day across orchestration systems and compute engines such as Titus, Spark, Trino, and Druid.

Technical Implementation: Someone still needs to find the useful signal in several logs, decide whether the cause sits in their code or the platform, and determine whether to retry, reconfigure, or escalate.
Deployment & Impact: Even a small share of difficult failures can consume engineering time, waste compute, and interrupt critical data pipelines.

stories.headline: Multi‑Ratio Video Resizing for Mobile Feed and Marketing
stories.summary: Serdar Cellat , Yuchen Xie , Bernadette Marcu , Blaid Burgess , Cody Jarrett , Carlos Pereira , Qing Shi , Samuel Carvajal , Manuel Pamplona , Dorothy Jung , Feiko Ritsema , Benjamin Klein , Alex Woo , Eugene Lok , Anna Pulido , Rebecka Swe , Sanford Holsapple , Ranjith Kumar Shetty Introduction Clips in the Netflix mobile app. At Netflix, a crucial part of our mission is ensuring our content looks stunning on any device.
stories.why_it_matters: Vertical formats are increasingly important for Netflix, as we have 1.2B followers across our social media accounts, and have recently rolled out Clips , our vertical video feed in the Netflix mobile app. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in big tech.
key_points: Problem & Context: Traditionally, creating vertical assets meant editors and producers manually reframed horizontal videos in editing tools, a process that doesn’t scale as our catalog and use cases grow.

Technical Implementation: To support both our in‑app feed and external marketing campaigns at scale, we built an automated multi‑ratio video cropping system, tightly integrated into our internal production tools, that can generate high‑quality vertical and other aspect‑ratio variants with minimal manual effort.

Deployment & Impact: Vertical formats are increasingly important for Netflix, as we have 1.2B followers across our social media accounts, and have recently rolled out Clips , our vertical video feed in the Netflix mobile app.

stories.headline: Tech Firms Dismantle Botnet That Turned 1.3M TV Boxes Into Proxies
stories.summary: Advertisement Skip to content HOMEABOUT THE AUTHOR ADVERTISING/SPEAKING Tech Firms Dismantle Botnet That Turned 1.3M TV Boxes Into Proxies November 2, 2026 0 Comments Google said today it worked with industry partners to dismantle a botnet made up of more than 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes that ship with malicious software which secretly rents the user’s Internet connection out to strangers and conducts advertising fraud. Experts involved in the takedown say the action is likely to sever the botnet’s access to more than 10 million additional compromised systems, including other Internet of Things (IoT) products such as Android-based healthcare devices and karaoke machines.
stories.why_it_matters: A report from the Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) said Google has severed ties with Videostrong Technology Co., a TV box manufacturer in China that GTIG and other industry experts concluded was responsible for including malware that enrolled more than 1.3 million set-top boxes in a botnet dubbed “XCPE” (named after one of the malware’s core code components). This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in cybersecurity.
